open_points.subject: A1 placement of previously placed content after it becomes a conflict copy
open_points.text:
A repeated placement returns it and writes nothing (P-06).
placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent`
open_points.question: When a placement for the hash already exists but the only current source with that hash is named as a Syncthing conflict copy, must the call return the existing placement or fail with `not_ready_or_absent`?
options: Return the existing placement because repeated placement is source-independent and writes nothing.
Fail with `not_ready_or_absent` because the current source is a conflict copy.
Return the existing placement only if the caller can prove that the original placement was made from a non-conflict name.
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing placement, preserving P-06 idempotency.

witness.initial: An ordinary file with source hash H was placed, so M04 contains its placement; afterward the ordinary file is gone and a file whose name contains `.sync-conflict-` has the same bytes and hash H.
events: The calling flow asks the deliverer to place source hash H again.
outcomes: The deliverer returns the existing placement and writes nothing, as P-06 and M04 require.
The deliverer refuses with `not_ready_or_absent`, as the new INV-18 Required tests passage requires for placement by the conflict copy's hash.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees either a placement result or a refusal.

open_points.subject: A1 placement when eligible and conflict-copy files share content
open_points.text: placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent`
open_points.question: If an ordinary eligible file and an ignored conflict copy have the same content hash, does placement by that hash succeed using the ordinary file, or does the presence of the conflict copy require refusal?
options: Succeed using the ordinary eligible file; the ignored path contributes no candidate.
Refuse because the requested hash also identifies a conflict copy.
Refuse only when every file with the hash is ignored.
open_points.default_guess: Succeed when at least one non-ignored eligible file has the hash.

witness.initial: The photo folder contains `photo.jpg` and `photo.sync-conflict-20261118.jpg` with identical bytes and hash H.
events: The calling flow scans the folder.
The calling flow requests placement of H.
outcomes: The scan reports `photo.jpg`, omits the conflict copy, and placement succeeds from `photo.jpg`.
Placement fails with `not_ready_or_absent` because a conflict copy has hash H.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees either a successful placement or `not_ready_or_absent`.

open_points.subject: INV-18 Required tests
open_points.text: a conflict copy, in the folder or a subfolder and in either letter case, is absent from the scan and placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent`
open_points.question: Which combinations must the witness test demonstrate: every root/subfolder and lower/upper/mixed-case combination, one case from each alternative, or only one representative combination?
options: Test the Cartesian product of root versus subfolder and lower, upper, and mixed-case marker spellings.
Test root and subfolder plus two representative letter-case spellings without requiring every combination.
One representative conflict-copy path is sufficient.
open_points.default_guess: Test root and subfolder and include lower-, upper-, and mixed-case spellings so the stated invariant is actually demonstrated.

witness.initial: The implementation ignores a lowercase marker in the root but fails to ignore an uppercase or mixed-case marker in a subfolder.
events: The Required test exercises only a lowercase conflict-copy name in the root.
A later user scan encounters an uppercase conflict-copy name in a subfolder.
outcomes: The Required test is considered sufficient and passes even though the later conflict copy is reported.
The Required test is considered incomplete because it did not demonstrate the stated location and case variants.
witness.observer: The test suite and the owner performing the later scan see the difference.

open_points.subject: R0-14 rename versus A1 ignored-name rule
open_points.text:
The file stays in the folder, and the owner who wants that version renames it, after which it is an ordinary photo.
A name is ignored, in any letter case and at every level of the path, when it begins with a dot or
with `~syncthing~`, ends in `.tmp` or `~`, or contains `.sync-conflict-`, the mark of a Syncthing
conflict copy (R0-14).
open_points.question: Does any rename make the copy an ordinary photo, or must the new name remove every ignored-name marker, especially `.sync-conflict-`?
options: It becomes ordinary only when the resulting name no longer matches any ignored-name rule.
Any owner rename clears conflict-copy treatment even if the new name still contains `.sync-conflict-`.
A separate provenance flag, rather than the resulting name, decides whether it remains a conflict copy.
open_points.default_guess: Require the resulting name to stop matching all ignored-name rules.

events: The owner renames it to `chosen.sync-conflict-20261118.jpg` without removing the marker.
outcomes: R0-14 makes the renamed file an ordinary photo, so the scan reports it.
A1 still classifies the resulting name as ignored, so the scan omits it.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the renamed file is offered.

open_points.subject: A1 ignored conflict-copy marker
open_points.text:
A name is ignored, in any letter case and at every level of the path, when it begins with a dot or
with `~syncthing~`, ends in `.tmp` or `~`, or contains `.sync-conflict-`, the mark of a Syncthing
conflict copy (R0-14).
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The `.sync-conflict-` policy value must become a provider-data constant named through `the imported X constant` (or be kept as a design fact outside the generated specification), rather than reaching generated code only as an inline prose literal.
